items.headline: Most teens worldwide don't get enough exercise

items.headline: High prices send more Americans to libraries
items.summary: Some Americans squeezed by the cost of living are leaning more on public libraries. Patrons are borrowing books and streaming services as well as items like instruments and sewing machines.

items.headline: Why schools still resist evidence-based reading methods
items.summary: Reporter Emily Hanford discusses why more teachers are not using proven methods for teaching children to read. The interview looks at the gap between research and classroom practice.

digest.overview:
Alaskans are still waiting on ballots in the U.S. Senate race and the open governor's race, and both contests could go to ranked-choice tabulation. Democrats, set to control both chambers of Congress, are expected to open investigations into Elon Musk, including his leadership of DOGE and his companies' federal contracts. The results reshaped the political map in the South, where Democratic wins in Texas and South Carolina put the region at the center of both parties' 2028 plans. Deb Haaland's win in New Mexico made her the first Native American woman elected governor, one of several historic firsts, and progressive William Lawrence unseated Republican Rep. Tom Barrett in Michigan's 7th District. Former baseball All-Star Mark Teixeira won a U.S. House seat in Texas. Voters in dozens of states decided 146 ballot measures on abortion, LGBTQ rights, guns, wealth taxes and redistricting. A global study found most teenagers do not get enough exercise, with girls lagging furthest behind. Squeezed by high prices, more Americans are turning to public libraries.

Abroad, a British court convicted Russell Brand of rape and sexual assault; the 51-year-old had denied the charges. Cristiano Ronaldo retired from Portugal's national team, ending a career that included six World Cups, a European title and the men's international scoring record. Bob Dylan met Pope Leo XIV at the Vatican during a break in his Italian tour. In China, an executive at electric carmaker BYD described the costs of the company's rapid global expansion amid trade tensions.

home.overview:
Jacksonville forced three turnovers and routed Baltimore 33–10 on Thursday night, moving to 6-2 atop the AFC South as the injury-ravaged Ravens lost a fourth straight behind rookie Joe Fagnano, who threw for 60 yards and two interceptions. Baltimore has agreed to trade for Arizona's Jacoby Brissett, Minnesota will start Carson Wentz on Monday night against Buffalo, and Sunday opens with Bengals–Falcons in the International Series. In the NBA, Stephen Curry hit six 3-pointers and scored 29 as Golden State beat Miami 120–100, and Devin Booker's 30 carried Phoenix past Orlando 117–104. Nine games are on tonight, led by 8-1 Philadelphia at Cleveland. In baseball, Tampa Bay exercised Drew Rasmussen's $20 million option.

Cristiano Ronaldo retired from Portugal's national team after 146 goals in 234 games. Bournemouth won 3–1 at Sparta Praha and Ferencváros won 2–0 at Milan to join Benfica on a perfect record in the Europa League, while Brighton won 1–0 at Getafe in the Conference League. Thomas Tuchel handed Jobe Bellingham a first England call-up. The weekend brings Atlético v Barcelona, Crystal Palace v Liverpool and MLS Decision Day, and FC Seoul host Ulsan HD in K League 1. In the KBO, Game 3 of the Korean Series, tied 1–1, was under way in Daegu, with KT missing two injured regulars from its lineup.

brief: Game 3 of the Korean Series, tied 1–1, began Friday evening in Daegu with Samsung's Ariel Jurado facing KT's So Hyeong-jun.
KT leadoff hitter Choi Won-jun sat out with a swollen left thumb after hitting a wall in Game 2, and third baseman Heo Kyoung-min was benched with chest spasms.
Samsung catcher Kang Min-ho is playing through an injury in the series.
Games 4 and 5 are afternoon games in Daegu on Saturday and Sunday, with Games 6 and 7, if needed, in Suwon next Tuesday and Wednesday.
